article.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
article.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

article.description: Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

article.description: Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the OVP confidential fund releases may have helped prevent rebel attacks.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential fund releases to the founding anniversaries of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) and the National Democratic Front (NDF), suggesting the funds may have helped prevent rebel attacks. On the 13th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Padilla questioned prosecution witness Roderick Wamil about three P125 million confidential fund checks issued in late 2022 and early 2023. Wamil is the former state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) who audited the P500 million confidential funds released to the OVP in four 125 million increments, as well as the P112.5 million for the Department of Education (DepEd) released in three checks worth 37.5 million each. “Itong pong mga dates na ito, nung December 26, March 29, April 24, lahat po ito walang nangyaring attack. Lahat po foiled. Wala po. For the first time, wala pong nangyaring attack. Kasi tuwing founding anniversary, may attack,” Padilla said. “On all of these dates, December 26, March 29, April 24, there were no attacks. Every single one was foiled. There’s none. For the first time, there were no attacks because every time the CPP-NPA celebrates its founding anniversary, there is usually an attack.” Padilla said in Filipino. When he started his clarificatory questions to the witness, Padilla referred to the first check for the OVP and asked, “Yung una pong cheke ay 125 million, December 20, 2022. article.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
article.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. article.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Counter-insurgency programs (P9.375 million in Q1; P9.3 million in Q2; P9.2 million in Q3)

  • Anti-illegal activities operations (P9 million in Q1; P9.1 million in Q2; P9.14 million in Q3)
  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. articles.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica, as the two people with the clearest knowledge of how the funds were handled and spent. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. Public officials entrusted with confidential funds must account for how public money was spent,” she said in an online press briefing on Thursday. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

articles.description: Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Counter-insurgency programs (P9.375 million in Q1; P9.3 million in Q2; P9.2 million in Q3)
  • Abuse prevention and control within schools (P10 million in Q1; P10.075 million in Q2; P10.125 million in Q3)
  • Anti-illegal activities operations (P9 million in Q1; P9.1 million in Q2; P9.14 million in Q3)
  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

articles.description: Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the OVP confidential fund releases may have helped prevent rebel attacks.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential fund releases to the founding anniversaries of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) and the National Democratic Front (NDF), suggesting the funds may have helped prevent rebel attacks. On the 13th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Padilla questioned prosecution witness Roderick Wamil about three P125 million confidential fund checks issued in late 2022 and early 2023. Wamil is the former state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) who audited the P500 million confidential funds released to the OVP in four 125 million increments, as well as the P112.5 million for the Department of Education (DepEd) released in three checks worth 37.5 million each. “Itong pong mga dates na ito, nung December 26, March 29, April 24, lahat po ito walang nangyaring attack. Lahat po foiled. Wala po. For the first time, wala pong nangyaring attack. Kasi tuwing founding anniversary, may attack,” Padilla said. “On all of these dates, December 26, March 29, April 24, there were no attacks. Every single one was foiled. There’s none. For the first time, there were no attacks because every time the CPP-NPA celebrates its founding anniversary, there is usually an attack.” Padilla said in Filipino. article.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
article.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. Prosecution

article.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. output.original_text: 'NAKARATING NA PO BA KAYO NG BARMM?' Senator-judge Robinhood Padilla asked former state auditor Roderick Wamil if he had ever visited the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) and whether he was aware of the country's ongoing terrorism threats. During his interjection, Padilla raised preliminary questions about the Audit Observation Memorandum, trying to establish ties to the confidential funds used by Vice President Sara Duterte for surveillance on potential New People's Army (NPA) recruitment. "Pero kayo po ang humahawak ng imbestigasyon patungkol sa confidential funds, tama po ba?" Padilla asked Wamil. "Hindi po siya imbestigasyon. Evaluation po," the witness answered. "Kayo po ba ay naniniwala na ang mga confidential agent ay dapat magpakilala? Sabihin ang kanilang totoong pangalan," the senator furthered. "Wala pong provisions as to that po sa joint circular," Wamil said. Padilla then asked Wamil to define "confidential," to which the auditor replied, "classified."
